devnet: isolate datadirs and genesis
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/30

Fixes #29.

## Summary

This closes the devnet/testnet cross-open hole by making devnet a distinct chain and by stamping datadirs with an explicit chain mode.

Changes:

- add a runtime-scoped devnet genesis, so devnet has a different genesis block id from canonical testnet/mainnet
- add a `chain_mode` metadata marker for `devnet` and `networked` datadirs
- reject `exfer node` / `mine` opening a devnet-marked datadir
- reject `exfer devnet` opening an existing networked or unmarked chain datadir
- force a one-time full `replay_chain` before stamping legacy unmarked networked datadirs as `networked`
- make wallet local/RPC send paths enter devnet mode when their datadir is devnet-marked, so `sig_message()` binds signatures to the devnet genesis
- document the new devnet isolation behavior

## Why

Before this change, a testnet build could:

1. run `exfer devnet` and create a chain with coinbase maturity 1
2. reopen the same datadir with `exfer node --datadir ...`
3. fast-open the chain without replaying per-transaction validation

That allowed a networked node process to run with history invalid under the canonical 360-block coinbase maturity rule.

The shared genesis also meant devnet-signed transactions had the same genesis-id signature binding as testnet/mainnet. A distinct devnet genesis fixes that root cause too.

## Validation

- `cargo test --features testnet`
- `cargo build`
- manual CLI checks before commit:
  - devnet datadir is refused by `exfer node`
  - networked datadir is refused by `exfer devnet`
  - legacy unmarked networked datadir gets one-time replay, then is stamped
